activities.question: Explain the main idea of Chapter 5.
activities.instructions: Use the source-based options to complete this activity.

correctItems.text: At the time of Mendel, the nature of those 'factors' regulating the pattern of inheritance was not clear.
In class XI you have learnt that nucleic acids are polymers of nucleotides.
Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA) are the two types of nucleic acids found in living systems.
DNA acts as the genetic material in most of the organisms.

activities.question: Arrange key steps or ideas from Chapter 5 in order.
activities.instructions: Use the source-based options to complete this activity.

correctItems.text: The length of DNA is usually defined as number of nucleotides (or a pair of nucleotide referred to as base pairs) present in it.
5.1.1 Structure of Polynucleotide Chain Let us recapitulate the chemical structure of a polynucleotide chain (DNA or RNA).
A nucleotide has three components - a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar (ribose in case of RNA, and deoxyribose for DNA), and a phosphate group.
There are two types of nitrogenous bases - Purines (Adenine and Guanine), and Pyrimidines (Cytosine, Uracil and Thymine).
